# Feed native Form cards through persisted Flutter snapshots

## Platform difference

An OH home-screen Form has a native lifecycle separate from the running Flutter widget tree.

## Implementation

NJU computes course JSON in Flutter, sends it through a channel, persists it natively, tracks form IDs and updates Form data. Pica Comic applies a similar snapshot/action bridge to reading history, buffering incoming actions until Dart handlers are ready. NJU introduces typed form data and attempts refresh scheduling; its prior study flags a mismatch between the epoch-seconds argument it constructs and the relative-minute API contract.

## Applicability

Use a stable payload model and a native initial response so the card can render while Flutter is absent. The NJU scheduling caveat is inherited source/API analysis, not a device-reproduced failure; check the API contract for the chosen SDK.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A native refresh callback reading saved data does not independently compute tomorrow's Flutter dataset. Bugaoshan disabling its home-widget feature does not establish that OH cards are impossible; these other projects implement a native route.

## Verification

Test card addition with the app closed, data freshness across day boundaries, typed schema changes, refresh interval units, multiple form IDs, action delivery and card removal.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
